However I do take issue with your case heat evaluation ..... Both cards actually dissipate the same amount of heat energy in watts, the TUF just gets it away from the GPU more efficiently however that doesn't actually affect how much total heat energy is dumped into the case, 300 watts of heat energy is still 300 watts of heat energy. In reality the FE will actually dump less heat energy into the case because a portion of the heat produced is actually dumped out the back .... In other words you actually need better case ventilation for the TUF than for the FE because it dumps 100% of the heat energy into the case while the FE doesn't ...... I'll be interested in seeing GN's analysis of the the FE to better determine exactly how much heat goes out the rear vent in percentages .... I'm guessing around 30%

At 2:57 you show the power draw being under 550, but you need to remember power supplies cannot output their entire rated wattage at once to the motherboard, cpu, and gpu. Part of the rated wattage is along other rails meant for sata power and the like. Also, power supply efficiency is a thing. For a system pulling nearly 550 watts I wouldn’t want anything less than a 750 watt power supply, as you should always have 100 watts of headroom on the power supply, and preferably 200 or more to get a better efficiency. Their ratings are accurate. Nvidia also mentioned their new cards can change power draw much more rapidly than previous cards could, which can be harder on power supplies. All the more reason not to get a budget power supply, or even use a precious power supply that’s been running for more than 4-5 years.
Nvidia doesn’t make power supplies, they have no marketing reason to sell more PSU’s and seem to have good reasoning behind it.
